subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic Gateway receive timestamp to agent-visible inbound metadata, and what field name, timestamp representation, and propagation boundary should be canonical?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but choosing a public cross-channel field and deciding whether it belongs in prompt metadata, SDK context, diagnostics, or all of them is maintainer API/product intent.

options.title: Add a generic receipt timestamp
options.body: Expose a single cross-channel field such as `gatewayReceivedAt` in the chosen metadata block and carry it through SDK/channel ingress with tests for at least one durable and one direct path.

options.title: Keep Timing Internal
options.body: Expose receive-to-dispatch timing in logs, diagnostics, or telemetry instead of adding another agent-visible prompt metadata field.

options.title: Defer To Channels
options.body: Let individual channel plugins add timing where needed, accepting less consistent cross-channel latency analysis.

recommendation.title: Add a generic receipt timestamp
recommendation.body: Expose a single cross-channel field such as `gatewayReceivedAt` in the chosen metadata block and carry it through SDK/channel ingress with tests for at least one durable and one direct path.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is closest to adjacent message metadata history and cross-channel API/product boundary work.
